cell_type_model: THP-1 and U937 promonocytic cells, primary monocytes/granulocytes, purified CD11b/CD18
assay_or_perturbation: fluorescent and radioiodinated haptoglobin binding, anti-CD11b/CD18 inhibition, purified receptor binding
relation_type: Direct haptoglobin binding to the Mac-1 alphaM-beta2 receptor complex; the alphaM subunit contribution was demonstrated but autonomous ITGAM was not isolated
pathway_branch: Haptoglobin -> Mac-1/alphaM-beta2 adhesion and acute-phase ligand recognition; no defined intracellular relay
limitations: The study supports direct binding to purified CD11b/CD18 and antibody-sensitive alphaM/beta2 participation, but describes low-affinity binding and does not establish a unique intracellular relay or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: THP-1 and U937 promonocytic cells, primary monocytes/granulocytes, purified CD11b/CD18
assay_or_perturbation: fluorescent and radioiodinated haptoglobin binding, anti-CD18 inhibition, purified Mac-1 binding
relation_type: Receptor-complex binding edge involving the beta2-containing Mac-1 receptor; ITGB2 is not claimed to act as an autonomous receptor
pathway_branch: Haptoglobin -> Mac-1/alphaM-beta2 adhesion and acute-phase ligand recognition; no defined intracellular relay
limitations: Anti-CD18 partially inhibited binding and purified Mac-1 bound haptoglobin, but the beta2 subunit was not tested as an isolated ligand receptor and no downstream relay was measured.

cell_type_model: Human LRP/CD91 affinity-purification and COS-cell reconstitution; cultured monocytes; murine intracerebral-hemorrhage models
assay_or_perturbation: ligand-affinity purification, Biacore binding, radiolabeled hemopexin-heme uptake, LRP1 expression/reconstitution, and LRP1-dependent heme-oxygenase-1 transcription
relation_type: Hemopexin-heme is captured and internalized by LRP1/CD91 as a scavenging/transport complex
pathway_branch: Hemopexin-heme -> LRP1/CD91 -> endocytosis and heme handling -> heme-oxygenase-1 response
limitations: The receptor-defined ligand is hemopexin-heme rather than apo-Hpx alone; LRP1-mediated uptake and heme handling are not a canonical ligand-triggered kinase relay and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human innate immune-cell models, H9C2 cardiomyoblasts, and mouse tumor/cachexia models
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant extracellular Hsp70 stimulation, TLR4 knockdown or siRNA, dominant-negative TLR4, kinase inhibitors, phosphoprotein assays, cytokine and catabolism readouts
relation_type: Extracellular Hsp70 activates a TLR4-dependent innate relay with Akt/ERK/JNK or MyD88-p38-NF-kappaB outputs
pathway_branch: Hsp70 -> TLR4-associated MyD88/p38/NF-kappaB and PI3K-AKT/ERK/JNK branches -> inflammatory cytokines and catabolic function
limitations: Receptor dependence is strong, but direct purified Hsp70-TLR4 molecular binding is not isolated in every study and Hsp70 preparations, co-receptors, and contaminant controls affect interpretation. No terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human endothelial and vascular smooth-muscle perlecan preparations; BaF3 cells expressing FGFR1b/c; primary vascular-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: perlecan isolation and glycosaminoglycan analysis, FGF2/FGFR1 ternary binding, FGFR1-expressing BaF3 growth, and endothelial/smooth-muscle signaling assays
relation_type: Perlecan presents or modulates FGF2-FGFR1 receptor-complex signaling, but a direct autonomous HSPG2-FGFR1 molecular edge was not isolated
pathway_branch: HSPG2/perlecan HS chains + FGF2 -> FGFR1 complex -> growth-factor signaling and vascular-cell proliferation
limitations: The strongest evidence is for perlecan-bound FGF2 and FGFR1 activation; source, sulfation, and glycosaminoglycan composition alter activity, so pathway-level ternary evidence was not promoted to direct HSPG2-FGFR1 binding.

cell_type_model: recombinant/engineered CALCR-RAMP3 amylin-3 receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: CALCR extracellular-loop mutagenesis, amylin and related peptide stimulation, cAMP accumulation, and ERK phosphorylation
relation_type: IAPP/amylin activates the CALCR-containing AMY3 receptor complex; CALCR is the signaling GPCR subunit
pathway_branch: IAPP -> CALCR/RAMP3 AMY3 receptor -> Gs-cAMP and ERK branches
limitations: The study uses engineered receptor complexes and focuses on how RAMP3 changes CALCR ligand binding and signal propagation; it does not establish a terminal TF or an autonomous CALCR-only response.

cell_type_model: recombinant/engineered CALCR-RAMP3 amylin-3 receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: RAMP3 coexpression with CALCR, CALCR loop mutagenesis, amylin stimulation, cAMP accumulation, and ERK phosphorylation
relation_type: Receptor-complex edge: IAPP activates the heteromeric CALCR/RAMP3 AMY3 receptor; RAMP3 is an accessory subunit rather than an autonomous receptor
pathway_branch: IAPP -> CALCR/RAMP3 AMY3 receptor -> cAMP and ERK signal propagation
limitations: RAMP3-dependent effects were measured in the heteromeric AMY3 receptor context and should not be interpreted as direct IAPP binding to isolated RAMP3; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Purified LFA-1/ICAM-1 systems, activated lymphocytes, Jurkat or BAF lymphoid transfectants, and primary neutrophils
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-1 binding and adhesion assays, LFA-1 conformational/activation studies, Rap1/PKC/PI3K perturbation, Src-family kinase inhibition, actin and transmigration readouts
relation_type: ICAM-1 binds the complete LFA-1 alphaL-beta2 complex and ligand engagement supports receptor-proximal outside-in cytoskeletal signaling
pathway_branch: ICAM1 -> LFA-1/ITGAL-ITGB2 -> Src-family/Rap1-actin adhesion and leukocyte transmigration
limitations: The exact receptor is the complete alphaL-beta2 complex and integrin activation depends on valency, cations, force, and cell state; pathway and migration outputs do not establish a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Purified Mac-1/ICAM-1 systems, primary neutrophils/monocytes, CD11b-transfected cells, and flow-adhesion models
assay_or_perturbation: Mac-1 binding and ICAM-1 adhesion assays, activation-specific antibody inhibition, CD11b mutant analysis, shear-flow adhesion, phagocytosis and cytokine readouts
relation_type: ICAM-1 binds the Mac-1 alphaM-beta2 complex and supports activation-state-dependent outside-in adhesion and myeloid-cell function
pathway_branch: ICAM1 -> Mac-1/ITGAM-ITGB2 -> integrin outside-in cytoskeletal/phagocytic and migration branch
limitations: Mac-1 contributions vary with activation state, shear, and competing ligands; the evidence supports the complete alphaM-beta2 complex rather than either subunit alone and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: L-cell integrin transfectants, purified ICAM-2/LFA-1 systems, endothelial monolayers, and primary leukocyte adhesion/crawling models
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-2 crystal/binding studies, antibody-blocking adhesion assays, force-dependent single-bond measurements, and transendothelial migration assays
relation_type: ICAM-2 binds the complete LFA-1 alphaL-beta2 complex and supports beta2-integrin adhesion and outside-in cytoskeletal relay
pathway_branch: ICAM2 -> LFA-1/ITGAL-ITGB2 -> integrin avidity, actin remodeling, and leukocyte transmigration
limitations: ICAM-2 binding is defined for complete LFA-1 and varies with species, activation state, and mechanical loading; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human red-cell ICAM-4, activated platelets, and alphaIIb-beta3-expressing transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-4-Fc adhesion, alphaIIb-beta3 activation, domain deletion and point-mutant mapping, peptide competition, and platelet blocking assays
relation_type: Direct binding of ICAM-4 to activated alphaIIb-beta3; the queue names the ITGA2B subunit of the receptor complex
pathway_branch: ICAM4 -> activated alphaIIb-beta3 adhesion and platelet/erythrocyte contact
limitations: Evidence is for the activated alphaIIb-beta3 complex, not autonomous ITGA2B; adhesion specificity was mapped but no receptor-proximal relay or terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: Human and mouse ICAM-4-Fc adhesion assays, alpha4beta1-expressing hematopoietic cells, and integrin-transfectant systems
assay_or_perturbation: peptide inhibition, alpha4beta1 antibody blockade, recombinant ICAM-4 adhesion, species-comparator assays, and later integrin-specific binding tests
relation_type: Conflicting receptor-complex evidence for ICAM-4-alpha4beta1; the exact ITGA4 subunit edge remains unresolved
pathway_branch: ICAM4 -> alpha4beta1 erythroblast adhesion comparator; conflicting alpha4beta1 versus beta2/beta3 receptor specificity
limitations: An early primary study reported alpha4beta1-dependent adhesion, while a later transfectant study failed to reproduce alpha4beta1 binding; no direct ITGA4-only assay or intracellular relay was found.

cell_type_model: Human red-cell ICAM-4 and alphaL-beta2 transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-4-Fc dose-dependent binding to alphaL-beta2 transfectants and integrin-specific antibody controls
relation_type: Direct ICAM-4 binding to the alphaL-beta2 receptor complex; the queue names the ITGAL subunit
pathway_branch: ICAM4 -> alphaL-beta2 adhesion; no isolated ITGAL relay
limitations: Binding was measured for complete alphaL-beta2 and the assay established receptor specificity, but ITGAL alone and a defined intracellular relay were not tested.

cell_type_model: Human red-cell ICAM-4, alphaM-beta2/CD11c-beta2 transfectants, monocyte/macrophage models
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-4-Fc binding and domain mapping, alphaM/alphaX-beta2 receptor transfectant assays, antibody inhibition, and erythrophagocytosis assays
relation_type: Direct ICAM-4 binding to beta2-containing alphaM/alphaX integrin complexes; the queue names the ITGAM subunit
pathway_branch: ICAM4 -> alphaM-beta2 or related beta2-integrin adhesion and erythrocyte clearance
limitations: The alphaM-specific contribution is supported in receptor-complex assays, but the exact alphaM-beta2 intracellular branch was not isolated for this pair and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human and mouse ICAM-4-Fc adhesion assays, alphaV-expressing cells, and alphaV-beta3 integrin transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: RGD/LDV peptide inhibition, antibody inhibition, recombinant ICAM-4 binding, and ICAM4 domain/point-mutant mapping
relation_type: Direct ICAM-4 binding to alphaV-family integrins, including alphaV-beta3; the queue names the ITGAV subunit
pathway_branch: ICAM4 -> alphaV-family integrin adhesion in erythroid and vascular-cell contexts
limitations: The measured receptors are alphaV-containing complexes rather than autonomous ITGAV; alphaV-beta3 binding sites differ from alphaIIb-beta3 sites and no intracellular relay or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human T cells, Jurkat cells, B-lymphoblastoid cells, rat hippocampal neurons, and purified LFA-1/ICAM-5 domains
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-5/Telencephalin adhesion assays, CD11a/CD18 antibody blockade, recombinant domain binding, and alphaL I-domain structural analysis
relation_type: Direct ICAM-5 binding to the alphaL-beta2 LFA-1 complex with neuronal-immune adhesion output
pathway_branch: ICAM5 -> LFA-1/ITGAL-ITGB2 -> T-cell-neuron adhesion; no defined intracellular relay
limitations: Binding is established for complete CD11a/CD18 and the first ICAM-5 domains; the queue names ITGAL and no autonomous alpha-chain relay or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human T cells, Jurkat cells, B-lymphoblastoid cells, rat hippocampal neurons, and purified LFA-1/ICAM-5 domains
assay_or_perturbation: ICAM-5/Telencephalin adhesion assays, CD11a/CD18 antibody blockade, recombinant domain binding, and alphaL I-domain structural analysis
relation_type: Receptor-complex binding edge involving the beta2-containing LFA-1 complex; ITGB2 is not an autonomous ICAM-5 receptor
pathway_branch: ICAM5 -> LFA-1/ITGAL-ITGB2 -> T-cell-neuron adhesion; no defined intracellular relay
limitations: Binding is established for complete CD11a/CD18, not isolated ITGB2; neuronal adhesion was measured but no beta2-specific intracellular relay or terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Primary mouse CD4 T-cell blasts, ICOSL-expressing antigen-presenting cells/AML cells, and bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells
assay_or_perturbation: ICOS or ICOSL costimulation, ICOSL overexpression/blockade, PI3K/AKT and MAPK assays, T-cell differentiation/cytokine assays, and ICOS-Ig reverse-signaling perturbation
relation_type: ICOSL ligation of ICOS provides receptor-proximal PI3K/MAPK costimulation; reverse ICOS-Ig-to-ICOSL signaling is retained as a distinct cellular branch
pathway_branch: ICOSL -> ICOS -> PI3K-AKT/MAPK and T-cell differentiation/cytokine outputs; reverse ICOSL p38-IL6 branch kept separate
limitations: Some mechanistic studies stimulate ICOS directly or use ICOSL overexpression, and reverse signaling through ICOSL is not forward ICOS signaling; no pair-specific terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Primary mouse mammary epithelial cells, human colon-carcinoma cells, and MCF-7 breast-cancer cells
assay_or_perturbation: IGF-I stimulation, IGF1R blockade or siRNA, receptor/IRS-1 phosphorylation, PI3K-AKT and ERK assays, and growth/survival perturbations
relation_type: IGF-I activates the IGF1R tyrosine-kinase receptor and recruits IRS-dependent PI3K-AKT and MAPK/ERK relay
pathway_branch: IGF1 -> IGF1R -> IRS1/2-PI3K-AKT and RAS-MAPK/ERK -> survival, proliferation, and differentiation outputs
limitations: The studies use heterogeneous epithelial and cancer models and downstream pathway activation is context dependent; no terminal TF was assigned from generic AKT/ERK output.

cell_type_model: Engineered cells expressing IR-A or IR-B without IGF1R, MCF-7 breast-cancer cells, and recombinant insulin-family receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: IGF-I binding/competition, insulin-receptor autophosphorylation, IRS-1/Akt/ERK assays, receptor isoform comparison, and mitogenic/survival readouts
relation_type: Low-affinity IGF-I activation of the insulin receptor is supported primarily for IR-A, with receptor-isoform-dependent signaling
pathway_branch: IGF1 -> INSR-A comparator -> IRS1/2, Akt, ERK, and p70S6K signaling
limitations: IGF-I is much weaker at INSR than IGF-II and the strongest evidence is for the IR-A isoform or atypical receptor contexts; the submitted INSR label does not specify isoform and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human and mouse receptor-expression systems and primary mouse mammary epithelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: IGF-II receptor binding, IGF1R or IR isoform comparison, receptor blockade, receptor phosphorylation, and IRS-1/PI3K-AKT signaling assays
relation_type: IGF-II binds and activates IGF1R and supports an IRS-dependent receptor-tyrosine-kinase relay
pathway_branch: IGF2 -> IGF1R -> IRS1/2-PI3K-AKT and MAPK/ERK mitogenic/survival branch
limitations: Relative IGF1R versus IR-A contribution depends on cell type and receptor abundance; the endpoint is a receptor pathway output rather than a pair-specific terminal TF.

cell_type_model: M6P/IGF2R receptor systems, engineered cells, and IGF2-dependent cancer-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: IGF-II and mannose-6-phosphate ligand binding, receptor internalization/trafficking, lysosomal degradation, and viability assays
relation_type: IGF2R/CI-MPR binds IGF-II mainly as a clearance and trafficking receptor rather than a canonical kinase-signaling receptor
pathway_branch: IGF2 -> IGF2R/CI-MPR -> endocytosis and lysosomal degradation -> reduced bioavailable IGF2
limitations: IGF2R lacks a canonical cytosolic kinase relay; viability effects reflect ligand depletion and lysosomal routing, not direct downstream TF activation.

cell_type_model: IR-A/IR-B engineered cells, fetal and cancer-cell receptor systems, and insulin-receptor signaling models
assay_or_perturbation: IGF-II receptor binding, IR-A autophosphorylation, IRS-1/Akt/ERK/p70S6K assays, receptor-isoform comparison, and proliferation/survival perturbations
relation_type: IGF-II binds and activates the insulin receptor predominantly through IR-A and produces a mitogenic receptor-tyrosine-kinase relay
pathway_branch: IGF2 -> INSR-A -> IRS1/2-Akt, ERK, PKC, and p70S6K -> mitogenic and survival outputs
limitations: The exact receptor isoform is essential: IR-A is the high-affinity IGF-II receptor, whereas IR-B is much less responsive; generic INSR evidence was not treated as isoform-independent and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Mouse cardiogenesis/cardiomyocyte models, 293-cell Wnt receptor assays, and Xenopus embryos/animal caps
assay_or_perturbation: IGFBP4 co-immunoprecipitation and binding to LRP6/FZD8, Wnt3A competition, LRP6 reporter assays, Igfbp4 knockdown, and cardiomyocyte differentiation
relation_type: Direct IGFBP4-LRP6 binding within an inhibitory FZD8-LRP6 Wnt receptor context; downstream Wnt antagonism is not an IGFBP4-activated kinase relay
pathway_branch: IGFBP4 -> FZD8/LRP6 receptor complex inhibition -> reduced canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling -> cardiogenesis
limitations: The study supports direct extracellular interaction and inhibition of Wnt3A binding, but not a receptor-proximal activating relay or a terminal TF; IGF sequestration also modifies the phenotype.

cell_type_model: Human cell-surface/secreted-protein interactome screen and purified extracellular DCC/IGFBPL1 proteins
assay_or_perturbation: pooled extracellular interactome screening, phylogenetic homology analysis, and SPR validation of DCC-IGFBPL1 binding
relation_type: Direct extracellular IGFBPL1-DCC binding; no DCC receptor-proximal relay or cellular functional output was established
pathway_branch: IGFBPL1-DCC extracellular interaction; DCC/netrin guidance biology remains a comparator pathway
limitations: The primary study validates an extracellular PPI in recombinant systems, but does not show ligand-induced DCC signaling, axon guidance, or a terminal TF for the exact pair.
